cycles.title: Frontiers of proof search and local exact compilation
cycles.objective: Expand the survivor registry while attacking proof-size versus proof-search confusion and testing whether local, certificate-based knowledge compilation can avoid the solve-and-encode loophole.
actions: Audited TC0-Frege proof-size and automatability frontiers.
Registered the polynomial-boundedness counterfrontier for full IPS on Boolean CNFs.
Separated proof existence, proof search, and proof verification in the registry.
Generated four restricted JANUS mechanisms for local d-DNNF compilation, parity extraction, residual quotienting, and proof-carrying elimination.
Rejected three circular or incomplete candidates into the permanent graveyard.
Generalized the validator to aggregate modular hypotheses, attacks, references, observations, journals, genealogies, and graveyard ledgers.
discoveries: TC0-Frege proof existence and TC0-Frege automatability must be tracked as separate questions.
Auxiliary variables and existential projection invalidate naive transfers of direct d-DNNF lower bounds.
The most promising refutation route for H016-H019 is a closure theorem showing that a semantic-diversity or communication lower bound survives their exact local certificate languages.
Locality alone is insufficient; bounded canonicalization and interface width are necessary to prevent hidden exponential work.
cycles.claim_boundary: No theorem, proof of P versus NP, novelty claim, or computational breakthrough was produced. All new entries remain R1 and OPEN only relative to the recorded attacks.
next_cycle: Instantiate a tiny concrete grammar for H016 and search exhaustively for its smallest counterexample.
Formalize an interface-communication measure preserved by the H018 and H019 certificate languages.
Choose explicit candidate tautology families for H012 and an explicit Boolean CNF family for H007.
Build a machine-readable incompatibility graph for mutually exclusive OPEN hypotheses.
